name: Vasa previa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Prenatal ultrasound diagnosis criteria for vasa previa

criteria.description: Identification of fetal blood vessels crossing or running near the internal cervical os on prenatal ultrasound
Demonstration of blood flow within unprotected fetal vessels overlying the cervix using color Doppler imaging
Fetal vessels not surrounded by placental tissue or umbilical cord substance (velamentous insertion)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fetal vessels crossing or near the internal cervical os with confirmed blood flow on color Doppler ultrasound
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily prenatal via targeted ultrasound; confirmation at delivery is definitive

pathognomonic.symptomName: Painless vaginal bleeding during third trimester
searchTerms: vaginal bleeding without pain in third trimester

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fetal heart rate abnormalities due to vessel compression or rupture
searchTerms: baby's heart rate changes from vessel pressure
fetal heartbeat problems due to vessel issues
abnormal fetal heart patterns from vessel rupture
signs of fetal distress on heart monitor
baby under stress detected by cardiotocography
abnormal fetal heart tracing indicating distress

occasional.notes: May be triggered by bleeding or membrane rupture

searchTerms: low blood pressure from heavy bleeding
drop in mother's blood pressure after bleeding
unusual attachment of umbilical cord to placenta

rare.notes: Due to vessel rupture and exsanguination

laboratory: Maternal blood type and antibody screen to assess for fetomaternal hemorrhage
Hemoglobin and hematocrit monitoring for maternal blood loss
imaging: Prenatal transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler demonstrating fetal vessels crossing the internal cervical os
other: Fetal heart rate monitoring showing decelerations or bradycardia
Delivery findings of unprotected fetal vessels overlying the cervix

distinguishingFeatures: Placental tissue covering internal cervical os rather than fetal vessels
Bleeding typically more profuse and may be painful
Premature separation of normally implanted placenta
Associated with abdominal pain and uterine tenderness

redFlags: Sudden painless vaginal bleeding in third trimester
Signs of fetal exsanguination or demise
references: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists Practice Bulletin No. 187: Vasa Previa
Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists Green-top Guideline No. 27: Placenta Praevia, Placenta Praevia Accreta and Vasa Praevia
